items.title: Early government modelling shows how long fuel stockpile lasts if imports slow
items.description: Diesel stocks would last about six months if Australia's imports dropped by 20 per cent, according to modelling compiled for the federal government early in the Middle East war.

items.title: Australia has not yet reached 'tipping point' for WFH directive, says expert
items.description: The fuel crisis is putting pressure on workers who rely on car travel and those who meet with vulnerable clients, with fresh calls for frontline support staff to be exempt from any future fuel rationing mandates.

items.title: RBA to remove surcharges on debit, credit cards and card networks
items.description: The removal of surcharges on debit and credit cards is one of the sweeping reforms from the Reserve Bank.

items.title: Live: Fuel excise won't alleviate impact of war, Albanese says
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese tells the ABC the government’s fuel excise "makes a difference" but will not "alleviate the impact of the war". Follow live.

items.title: NDIS agency hired 70pc of all new federal public servants last year
items.description: The agency that runs the National Disability Insurance Scheme defends hiring nearly 2,000 new employees last year despite major changes being rolled out to rein in the program's cost.

items.title: A minute before Trump's wild Iran claim, oil traders made 'abnormal' moves
items.description: Global stock markets, which for the past month have been remarkably restrained as the Middle East crisis unfolded, have begun to wobble.

items.title: Fair Work Commission abolishes junior pay rates for young adults
items.description: The Fair Work Commission has issued its decision to abolish junior pay rates for young adult employees in the retail, fast food, and pharmacy sectors while maintaining them for minors.

items.title: Live: Coalition grills PM over fuel crisis during Question Time
items.description: Anthony Albanese faces a grilling from MPs as energy minister provides fuel availability update.  Follow live.

items.title: What we know about where Dezi Freeman made his last stand
items.description: The rural property where police finally caught up with the fugitive gunman was a good place to disappear.

items.title: Telstra claims new coverage maps will 'make it much harder' for customers
items.description: ACMA has introduced new rules for standardised mobile coverage maps that will see mobile signals below -115 dBm labelled as "no coverage".

items.title: Jackie O claiming 'at least' $82m in legal action against ARN Media
items.description: Former Sydney radio broadcaster Jackie "O" Henderson has filed legal action against employer ARN Media, following the collapse of the hit Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: 'I'm sick of it': One in two Australians priced out of healthcare system
items.description: One in two Australians missed out on health care they needed last year mainly because they could not afford it, according to a new report by the peak healthcare consumers group.

items.title: Live: Consumer confidence hits 53-year low, ASX up, AUD flat
items.description: Consumer confidence across Australia has hit its worst level since tracking began in 1973, according to the latest ANZ-Roy Morgan survey, but the ASX 200 has bounced back to rise by almost 1 per cent. Follow the day's events on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: IOC's proposed gender test not fit for purpose, says man who discovered it
items.description: The scientist who discovered the SRY gene test that the International Olympic Committee is now relying on to determine athletes' eligibility for women's events says it should not be used in such a fashion.

items.title: Tim Rogers is an Aussie rock legend — that doesn't impress the bank
items.description: The frontman of ARIA Hall Of Famers You Am I on work, family, and why Hourly, Daily is still special to him.

items.title: What happens if your house is underinsured?
items.description: If your home is underinsured, it means your insurance policy won't fully cover the cost of rebuilding, repairing or replacing it.

items.title: Transphobia nearly killed Kaz. Now he just wants to be 'me'
items.description: This WA teenager was depressed, ill and missing out on school. He says it was part of the toll transphobia took on him.

items.title: Young farmers slash job times by swapping horses and quad bikes for drones
items.description: A shift towards modern technology is making a career in agriculture more appealing to a new generation of farmers.

items.title: Supermarket chicken could get cheaper due to grain breakthrough
items.description: Australian researchers develop a high-protein sorghum variety, hoping to replace expensive livestock feed with systems that could lead to cheaper meat and eggs.

items.title: Cobram Estate praises America's 'grower-first mentality' after $260m deal
items.description: Australia's largest olive oil producer has completed its purchase of a massive olive grove in California, giving it about 70 per cent of the state's production.

items.title: The 10 pivotal events that led to the downfall of Essendon and Carlton
items.description: Essendon and Carlton were once mainstays when it came to the business end of the AFL season. Over the last quarter century, both clubs have fallen on hard times. Here's why.

items.title: Businesses report increase in abuse from customers as fuel crisis worsens
items.description: From pile-on comments on social media to roadside slurs, local businesses are reminding their communities to "be kind to the little guy" amid the fuel crisis.

items.title: NASA begins countdown for humanity's first launch to the moon in 53 years
items.description: Four astronauts on the Artemis II rocket are set to blast off early Thursday morning.

items.title: Air Canada CEO to retire after English-only crash message draws criticism
items.description: Michael Rousseau sparked controversy for addressing a deadly crash in an English-only video with French subtitles.

items.title: Iran's 'safe passage' signals a new global divide
items.description: China is now the world's largest crude oil importer, and Iran — though a discounted and often opaque supplier — remains a consistent part of that supply mix.
